questions.question: Which organisation, established by the Indian government, serves as the regulatory and promotional body to facilitate increased private sector participation in India's space activities as of March 2025?

options.text: Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **IN-SPACe** was established by the **Government of India** to act as a regulatory and promotional body for private sector participation in **India's space activities**.
 
• It was announced by the Indian government in **June 2020** as part of reforms to open up the space sector to private players.
 
• IN-SPACe operates under the aegis of the **Department of Space (DoS)** and facilitates non-governmental entities in their engagement with space activities.
 
• The organization ensures the level playing field for private industries, universities, and startups to conduct space-related operations alongside the Indian Space Research Organisation (**ISRO**).
 
• Its primary role includes **authorization, promotion, and hand-holding of private sector entities** in space exploration, satellite development, and launch vehicle creation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):**

 
 
• ISRO is India's national space agency headquartered in **Bengaluru** and operates under the **Department of Space**.
 
• It was established in **1969** and is responsible for space exploration, satellite deployment, and development of launch vehicles.
 
• Key achievements include the **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)**, **Chandrayaan missions**, and the **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)**.
 
 
 
• **Department of Space (DoS):**
 
 
• The DoS oversees the space program in India and formulates policies related to space activities.
 
• It manages the coordination between various space organizations, including **ISRO** and **IN-SPACe**.
 
 
 
• **Space Applications Centre (SAC):**
 
 
• SAC is a major center of ISRO located in **Ahmedabad**, Gujarat.
 
• It specializes in the development of payloads for satellites and conducts research in areas such as communication, remote sensing, and space sciences.
 
 
 
• **Role of IN-SPACe:**
 
 
• IN-SPACe acts as a single-window mechanism to allow **private entities** to use ISRO’s facilities and technical expertise.
 
• It provides technical guidance and facilitates the sharing of infrastructure for satellite launches and manufacturing.
 
• It also ensures compliance with national security and international obligations while promoting private sector growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Space Sector Reforms in India:**

 
 
• In **2020**, the Government of India introduced reforms to encourage private sector participation in space activities.
 
• These reforms aim to develop a robust ecosystem for space technologies and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of IN-SPACe:**
 
 
• IN-SPACe functions as a bridge between **ISRO** and private companies, ensuring equitable access to space resources.
 
• It plays a crucial role in advancing India’s space exploration goals and developing indigenous capabilities for global competitiveness.

questions.question: The mandap of the temple is referred to as the 'Jagamohan' in which school of temple architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha School**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jagamohan** refers to the assembly hall or porch of a temple in the **Kalinga or Odisha School of temple architecture**. It serves as the area where devotees congregate before proceeding to the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha).
 
• The **Kalinga School**, which flourished in the region of modern-day Odisha, is renowned for its unique style, and the temples constructed in this tradition are characterized by their distinct architectural components.
 
• In Odisha temples, the **Jagamohan** is often rectangular or square in shape and is distinguished by its pyramidal roof structure, which is an essential feature of this architectural school.
 
• The **Jagamohan** is positioned in front of the sanctum and complements the main tower (shikhara or deul). These two structures together form the essential components of Odisha temples, such as the Sun Temple in Konark and the Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar.
 
• The Odisha School of temple architecture is particularly noted for its intricate carvings and detailed ornamentation, which extend to the **Jagamohan**, making it a significant architectural and cultural element.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of Odisha School of Architecture:**

 
 
• The temples typically consist of three major components: the **Deul (sanctum sanctorum)**, the **Jagamohan (assembly hall)**, and the **Natmandir (dance hall)**. The **Bhogmandir** (offering hall) is also an additional component in many cases.
 
• The **Deul** has a curvilinear spire (rekha deul) that rises vertically and tapers at the top. The **Jagamohan** is rectangular or square with a pyramidal roof, as mentioned earlier.
 
• The walls of the temples are adorned with **highly intricate carvings**, which include depictions of deities, mythical creatures, floral motifs, and scenes from epics like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.
 
• Prominent examples of this architectural style include the **Konark Sun Temple**, **Jagannath Temple** in Puri, and the **Lingaraja Temple** in Bhubaneswar.
 
 
 
• **Other Schools of Temple Architecture (Options Provided):**
 
 
• **Solanki School:** This school is associated with Gujarat and includes temples like the **Modhera Sun Temple**. It is characterized by its intricately carved toranas (arched gateways) and elaborate stepwells (vavs).
 
• **Pala School:** Flourishing in Bengal and Bihar under the Pala dynasty, this school emphasized **Buddhist architecture**. Monasteries like **Vikramashila** and **Somapura Mahavihara** are notable examples.
 
• **Khajuraho School:** Associated with the **Chandela dynasty** in Madhya Pradesh, it is renowned for its exquisite sculptures and erotic carvings. Temples like the **Kandariya Mahadev** and **Lakshmana Temple** are prominent examples.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Kalinga temples** are unique in their layout, consisting of a single axis with the sanctum, Jagamohan, and other components aligned in a linear pattern.
 
• The **Kalinga architecture** emphasizes verticality, with the **Deul** rising prominently above the rest of the structure.
 
• The **Jagamohan** serves both a functional and aesthetic purpose, providing space for rituals and enhancing the temple's grandeur.

questions.question: The H.C.F. and the L.C.M. of two numbers are 49 and 490, respectively. If one of the numbers is 245, find the other one.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that, Product of two numbers = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

⇒ 245 × Second Number = 49 × 490

⇒ Second Number = (49 × 490) ÷ 245

⇒ Second Number = 490 ÷ 5 = 98

**∴ The correct answer is 98.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

H.C.F. of two numbers = 49

L.C.M. of two numbers = 490

First number = 245

 H.C.F. = 49 L.C.M. = 490 First Number = 245 Second Number = ? × × = 
 
 

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

**Calculations:**

Let the second number be x.

⇒ 245 × x = 49 × 490

⇒ x = (49 × 490) ÷ 245

⇒ x = 490 ÷ (245 ÷ 49)

⇒ x = 490 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 98

**∴ The correct answer is 98.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Numbers Rule

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M. is always equal to the product of the numbers. Formula: a × b = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their H.C.F. is 1. The L.C.M. of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

Fractions H.C.F. & L.C.M.

H.C.F. of fractions = (H.C.F. of Numerators) ÷ (L.C.M. of Denominators). L.C.M. of fractions = (L.C.M. of Numerators) ÷ (H.C.F. of Denominators).

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 99 min and 90 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 50 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM(99, 90, 50) = 4950 units.

Efficiency of A = 4950 ÷ 99 = 50 units/min.

Efficiency of B = 4950 ÷ 90 = 55 units/min.

Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = 4950 ÷ 50 = 99 units/min.

Efficiency of C = 99 − (50 + 55) = −6 units/min.

Time taken by C = 4950 ÷ 6 = 825 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 825 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 99 min

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 90 min

Time taken by all three pipes (A + B + C) to fill the cistern = 50 min

**Concept Used:**

Total capacity = LCM of individual time taken

Efficiency = Total capacity ÷ Time taken

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of emptying Pipe C be E꜀.

⇒ Total Efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B + Efficiency of C

⇒ 99 = 50 + 55 + E꜀

⇒ 99 = 105 + E꜀

⇒ E꜀ = 99 − 105

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another can empty it in y hours (where y > x), then the net part of the tank filled in 1 hour is (1/x) − (1/y).

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done. If multiple people work for the exact same number of days, their wages are divided in the direct ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: The marked price of an iPad is ₹960. It is sold with two successive discounts of 25% each, followed by an additional 15% discount for cash payment. What is the final selling price (in ₹) after the cash discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The final Selling Price (SP) after successive discounts can be found directly using multiplying factors.

A 25% discount means the item is sold at 75% or 3/4 of its price.

A 15% discount means the item is sold at 85% or 17/20 of its price.

Final SP = 960 × (3/4) × (3/4) × (17/20)

Final SP = 960 × (153/320) = 3 × 153 = 459

**∴ The correct answer is ₹459.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the iPad = ₹960

Successive discounts: D₁ = 25%, D₂ = 25%, D₃ = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Final Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100) × (1 − D₃/100)

 
 Successive Discount Flow

⇒ SP = 960 × (75/100) × (75/100) × (85/100)

⇒ SP = 960 × (3/4) × (3/4) × (17/20)

Effective Equivalent Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is calculated using the formula: Equivalent Discount = (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the article. Meanwhile, Profit or Loss percentages are calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 90% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on marked price should be allowed to gain 71%?

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 90% = 190

Selling Price (SP) for 71% profit = 100 + 71% = 171

Discount = MP − SP = 190 − 171 = 19

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (19 ÷ 190) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the six fundamental rights provided in Part III of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Religious Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Constitution** guarantees six fundamental rights under **Part III**, which are essential for individual liberty and social equality. However, the **Right to Religious Education** is not explicitly mentioned as a fundamental right.
 
• The six fundamental rights include:
 
 
• **Right to Equality** (Articles 14–18): Ensures equality before the law and prohibits discrimination on various grounds.
 
• **Right to Freedom** (Articles 19–2: Includes freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• **Right against Exploitation** (Articles 23–2: Prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and child labor in hazardous employment.
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion** (Articles 25–28): Ensures religious freedom, including the right to profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• **Cultural and Educational Rights** (Articles 29–30): Protects the rights of minorities to preserve their culture and establish educational institutions.
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies** (Article 3: Empowers individuals to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• The **Right to Religious Education** is not explicitly recognized as a standalone fundamental right. However, **Article 28** under the **Right to Freedom of Religion** addresses religious instruction, stating that no religious instruction shall be provided in educational institutions wholly funded by the state.
 
• The **Right to Equality**, **Right against Exploitation**, and **Right to Freedom** are well-defined and form an integral part of the six fundamental rights.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Right to Religious Education**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Articles Related to Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• **Article 14:** Ensures equality before the law and equal protection of laws.
 
• **Article 19:** Provides six freedoms, including speech, assembly, and movement.
 
• **Article 23:** Prohibits human trafficking and forced labor.
 
• **Article 25:** Guarantees the freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• **Article 32:** Empowers individuals to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of rights.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Article 28:**
 
 
• No religious instruction is allowed in educational institutions wholly maintained out of state funds.
 
• Religious instruction is permitted in institutions administered by religious bodies but not funded by the state.
 
• Students cannot be compelled to attend religious instruction in institutions recognized by the state or receiving state aid.
 
 
 
• **Important Features of Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• They are justiciable, meaning individuals can move courts to enforce them.
 
• They aim to promote political democracy and prevent authoritarian rule.
 
• They are not absolute and are subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order, morality, and national security.
 
 
 
• **Key Differences:**
 
 
• The **Right to Religious Education** is not a separate fundamental right but is implicitly covered under the **Right to Freedom of Religion**.
 
• Educational rights for minorities under **Article 30** allow them to establish and administer their educational institutions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amendments to Fundamental Rights:** Fundamental rights can be amended by the Parliament, but the basic structure of the Constitution cannot be altered (as per the **Keshavananda Bharati case, 1973**).
 
• **Directive Principles vs Fundamental Rights:** While fundamental rights are enforceable, directive principles are non-justiciable but aim to achieve social and economic democracy.
 
• **Suspension During Emergency:** Fundamental rights under **Articles 19** can be suspended during a national emergency (Article 35, except for rights under Articles 20 and 21.

In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Question: Among 5 Sticks, M,A,N,C and G each having a different length, which stick is the longest?

Statements:

(I) M is shorter than A but longer than N.

(II) N is longer than C but shorter than G.

options.text: Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not.
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question.
Both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Five sticks: M, A, N, C, and G.

**From Statement (I):**

M is shorter than A but longer than N.

= A > M > N

(This tells us A is longer than M and N, but we don't know about C and G.)

**From Statement (II):**

N is longer than C but shorter than G.

= G > N > C

(This tells us G is longer than N and C, but we don't know about A and M.)

**Combining Statement (I) and (II):**

From (I): A > M > N

From (II): G > N > C

Combining them through the common stick N, we get: (A, M, G) > N > C.

While we know A is longer than M, there is no data to compare the lengths of **A** and **G**. Therefore, we cannot determine which one is the longest.

Thus, Both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question: With regard to their occupation, the early Vedic Aryans were _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pastoralists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The early Vedic Aryans were primarily **pastoralists**. Their economy was centered around cattle rearing, which was a symbol of wealth and status in their society.
 
• Cattle, especially cows, were considered sacred and vital for their livelihood. Products like milk, butter, and ghee were essential parts of their diet and rituals.
 
• The early Aryans were **semi-nomadic**, moving from one place to another in search of pastures and water for their cattle. This lifestyle shaped their culture, beliefs, and daily practices.
 
• Agriculture, though present, was not the primary occupation during the early Vedic period. It became more prominent later during the later Vedic age.
 
• Hunting and fishing were supplementary activities but did not constitute their main economic activities. The focus was on maintaining large herds of cattle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Early Vedic Society:**

 
 
• The early Vedic society was tribal and organized into clans or **janas**. Leadership was provided by chiefs, known as **rajas**, who protected the tribe and its cattle.
 
• Their lifestyle revolved around cattle rearing, which was central to their economy and culture. Cows were often used as a medium of exchange, highlighting their economic significance.
 
• The Rigveda, the oldest Vedic text, provides evidence of their pastoral lifestyle, with numerous hymns dedicated to cattle and their protection.
 
 
 
• **Religion and Rituals:**
 
 
• Religious practices were closely tied to nature. They worshipped deities like **Indra** (god of rain and war), **Agni** (fire god), and **Surya** (sun god), who were believed to protect their cattle and ensure prosperity.
 
• Animal sacrifices were common in rituals, and these practices were often intended to seek blessings for good pastures and the well-being of their herds.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Cattle:**
 
 
• Cattle were used for **plowing**, transportation, and as a source of milk and other dairy products.
 
• The term **“Gomat”**, meaning rich in cattle, was used as a compliment. Wealth was often measured in terms of the number of cattle owned.
 
• Conflicts between tribes often revolved around the ownership of grazing lands and cattle.
 
 
 
• **Transition to Agriculture:**
 
 
• While the early Vedic Aryans were primarily pastoralists, they gradually began practicing agriculture as they settled in the fertile plains of the Ganges and Yamuna.
 
• This transition marked the beginning of the later Vedic period, where agriculture became a more significant aspect of the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: Fishermen and hunters** - While hunting was a supplementary activity, it was not their primary occupation during the early Vedic period.
 
• **Option 2: Merchants and traders** - Trade and commerce were minimal during this period as the society was largely self-sufficient and semi-nomadic.
 
• **Option 3: Priests** - Priests were important in performing rituals and sacrifices, but they were not the primary economic contributors.
 
• **Option 4: Pastoralists** - This is the correct answer as cattle rearing formed the backbone of their economy and lifestyle.

• **Amravati, Bhavani, Hemavati, and Kabini** are the main tributaries of the **Kaveri River**, which is one of the major rivers of southern India.
 
• The **Kaveri River** originates from the **Brahmagiri Hills** of the Western Ghats in **Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka**.
 
• It flows through the states of **Karnataka** and **Tamil Nadu**, covering a total length of approximately **800 kilometers** before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The Kaveri River is significant for agriculture and is often referred to as the **"Ganga of the South"** due to its importance in irrigation and water supply in southern India.

questions.question: What is the term used for alternative forms of a gene?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allele**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Allele** refers to alternative forms of a gene that occur at the same locus on homologous chromosomes. These variations arise due to mutations and result in genetic diversity.
 
• An individual inherits two alleles for each gene—one from each parent. These alleles can be identical (homozygous) or different (heterozygous).
 
• Alleles can be classified as **dominant** or **recessive**, determining the expression of traits. A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele when paired together.
 
• The concept of alleles was first described by **Gregor Mendel** during his experiments on pea plants, forming the basis of modern genetics.
 
• Examples of alleles include the genes responsible for eye color, where variations like blue, brown, or green result from different alleles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Genome:**

 
 
• The genome represents the complete set of genetic material present in an organism, including all its genes and non-coding regions.
 
• It is organized into chromosomes and varies widely between organisms in terms of size and number of genes.
 
• The Human Genome Project, completed in **2003**, mapped the entire human genome, consisting of approximately **3 billion base pairs**.
 
 
 
• **Chromosome:**
 
 
• Chromosomes are thread-like structures made up of **DNA** and proteins (histones), found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
 
• Humans have **23 pairs of chromosomes**, including one pair of sex chromosomes (XX or XY).
 
• They carry genetic material that is crucial for inheritance, cellular functions, and development.
 
 
 
• **Locus:**
 
 
• A locus refers to the specific physical location of a gene or genetic marker on a chromosome.
 
• It is a fixed position, and alleles of a gene are found at the same locus on homologous chromosomes.
 
• Loci are often used in genetic mapping and studies to identify traits and diseases associated with particular genes.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Alleles in Genetics:**
 
 
• Alleles are fundamental to understanding heredity and genetic variation, as they determine traits such as height, color, and susceptibility to diseases.
 
• Genetic disorders like **Sickle Cell Anemia** and **Cystic Fibrosis** result from mutations in alleles.
 
• Research on alleles contributes to advancements in personalized medicine and genetic engineering.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gregor Mendel's Laws:**

 
 
• **Law of Segregation:** States that each individual has two alleles for a trait, and these alleles separate during gamete formation.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment:** States that alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation, contributing to genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Allele Research:**
 
 
• Allele study aids in identifying genetic predispositions to diseases such as **diabetes** and **cancer**.
 
• Allele-specific techniques are used in **CRISPR gene editing** for correcting genetic mutations.
 
• Population genetics studies use allele frequencies to understand evolutionary processes and migration patterns.

questions.question: Given the data set {x + 4, 2x - 3, 5x, x + 1, 3x + 2}, for x > 1, where x is a natural number, if the median is 7, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For questions involving the median of algebraic terms, the fastest approach is to test the given options directly.

Test Option 1 (x = 3):

Substitute x = 3 into the set {x + 4, 2x − 3, 5x, x + 1, 3x + 2}.

The values become {7, 3, 15, 4, 11}.

Arranging in ascending order gives: 3, 4, 7, 11, 15.

The middle term (median) is 7, which perfectly matches the question's given condition.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data set = {x + 4, 2x − 3, 5x, x + 1, 3x + 2}

Condition: x > 1, where x is a natural number.

Median = 7

**Formula Used:**

The median of an odd number of terms is the middle value when arranged in ascending order: ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.

 
• 1st 2nd Median 4th 5th 2x − 3 x + 1 x + 4 = 7 3x + 2 5x Ascending Order of Terms (For x = 3) 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of terms (n) = 5.

⇒ The median will be the 3rd term when sorted in ascending order.

⇒ Let's analyze the relative values of the given expressions for x > 1.

⇒ Clearly, 5x and 3x + 2 will be the largest terms in the set.

⇒ The three smallest terms are x + 1, 2x − 3, and x + 4.

⇒ If 2x − 3 were the median, 2x − 3 = 7 ⇒ x = 5. However, substituting x = 5 gives {9, 7, 25, 6, 17}, which has a median of 9, not 7.

⇒ Thus, x + 4 naturally takes the 3rd position and acts as the true median.

⇒ Equating the 3rd term to the given median: x + 4 = 7.

⇒ x = 7 − 4 = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median of Ungrouped Data

To find the median, arrange the data in ascending or descending order. If n is odd, the median is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term. If n is even, it is the average of the (n ÷ 2)th and (n ÷ 2 + 1)th terms.

Mean vs Median

The mean is sensitive to extreme values (outliers), whereas the median provides a more robust and stable measure of central tendency for skewed distributions.

Mode of Data

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a given data set. A dataset can have a single mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all if all values are unique.

• This statistic highlights the pervasive issue of **gender-based violence**, particularly within households, emphasizing the need for stronger global measures for women’s safety.
 
• Intimate partner violence is one of the most common forms of violence faced by women globally, as reported by multiple international agencies like the **UN Women** and **World Health Organization (WHO)**.
 
• Such killings often occur in the context of **domestic abuse**, reflecting systemic issues such as inequality, lack of legal protection, and societal norms that perpetuate violence against women.
 
• The data serves as a call to action for policymakers and governments to strengthen laws, provide support to victims, and implement awareness campaigns to combat this critical issue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gender-Based Violence:**

 
 
• **Gender-based violence** refers to harmful acts directed at individuals based on their gender. It includes physical, sexual, psychological, and economic abuse.
 
• According to the **UNODC**, women and girls are disproportionately affected by intimate partner violence compared to men.
 
• The **WHO** estimates that nearly **1 in 3 women** worldwide have experienced physical or sexual violence, mostly by their intimate partners.
 
 
 
• **Role of International Organizations:**
 
 
• **UN Women** works globally to promote gender equality and empower women, while addressing issues like violence and discrimination.
 
• The **United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)** collects and disseminates data on crime and justice, including gender-based violence statistics.
 
 
 
• **Legislation and Policies:**
 
 
• Many countries have implemented laws to protect women from domestic violence. For instance, India’s **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (2005)** offers legal remedies to victims.
 
• International treaties like the **Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW)** urge nations to address gender-based violence and discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Awareness Campaigns:**
 
 
• Global campaigns like the **UN’s “16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence”** aim to raise awareness about violence against women and promote actionable solutions.
 
• Programs like **HeForShe** encourage men and boys to advocate for gender equality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Regions such as **Asia** and **Africa** report higher rates of gender-based killings due to cultural and systemic factors.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Society:**

• It also hampers societal development and equality, creating barriers to achieving **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly **SDG 5** (Gender Equality).

BODMAS Rule

BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. It sets the standard order of operations to accurately solve mathematical expressions.

Types of Brackets

When multiplying a negative number by a positive number, the result is always negative (e.g., −a × b = −ab). Conversely, multiplying two negative numbers yields a positive result.

questions.question: A conical cap has the base diameter 40 cm and height 21 cm. What is the cost (rounded off to one decimal place) of painting the surface of the cap at the rate of 112 paise per sq. cm? (Use pi=(22)/(7))

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius (r = 20) and height (h = 21) form a standard Pythagorean triplet (20, 21, 29) with the slant height (l), so l = 29 cm.

A cap is open at the base, meaning we only need to calculate and paint the Curved Surface Area (CSA).

CSA = πrl = (22/7) × 20 × 29 cm²

Cost = CSA × Rate = (22/7) × 20 × 29 × 1.12 (since 112 paise = ₹1.12)

Cost = 22 × 20 × 29 × 0.16 = ₹ 2,041.6

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 2,041.6.**

Base diameter = 40 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 20 cm

Height (h) = 21 cm

Rate of painting = 112 paise/cm² = ₹1.12/cm²

**Formula Used:**

Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl

Total Cost = CSA × Rate

**Calculation:**

⇒ l = √(20² + 21²)

⇒ l = √(400 + 441) = √841 = 29 cm

⇒ CSA = (22/7) × 20 × 29

⇒ CSA = 12760/7 cm²

⇒ Total Cost = (12760/7) × 1.12

⇒ Total Cost = 12760 × (1.12/7)

⇒ Total Cost = 12760 × 0.16

⇒ Total Cost = 2041.6

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 2,041.6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

The volume represents the 3D space enclosed by a cone. Formula: V = (1/3)πr²h

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

This includes the curved surface and the solid circular base. Formula: TSA = πr(r + l)

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² help speed up calculations heavily. Examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (20, 21, 29).

What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

30, 40, 50, 60, 70, ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given number series follows a constant difference pattern.

Observe the difference between consecutive terms: 40 − 30 = 10, 50 − 40 = 10.

The common difference is +10.

Add 10 to the last known term to directly find the missing term: 70 + 10 = 80.

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Series:** 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, ?

**Pattern Logic:** Each term is formed by adding 10 to the preceding term, making it an Arithmetic Progression.

30 +10 → 40 +10 → 50 +10 → 60 +10 → 70 +10 → 80

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1st term = 30

⇒ 2ⁿd term = 30 + 10 = 40

⇒ 3rd term = 40 + 10 = 50

⇒ 4th term = 50 + 10 = 60

⇒ 5th term = 60 + 10 = 70

⇒ 6th term (?) = 70 + 10 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (A.P.)

A sequence of numbers where the difference between any two consecutive terms remains constant. The nth term is calculated as Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where 'a' is the first term and 'd' is the common difference.

Double Difference Series

When the primary differences between terms are not identical, calculating the differences of the primary differences will frequently uncover the underlying pattern in complex number series.

questions.question: Three years ago from now, Aman was four times Chaman's age. Three years from now, he will be twice as old as Chaman. What is Aman's current age (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Aman to Chaman 3 years ago = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 parts)

Ratio 3 years from now = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 part) → Multiply by 3 to equate difference → 6 : 3

Increase in ratio for Aman = 6 − 4 = 2 parts, corresponding to a total gap of 6 years.

2 parts = 6 years → 1 part = 3 years.

Aman's age 3 years ago = 4 parts = 12 years → Present age = 12 + 3 = 15 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Aman's age 3 years ago = 4 × Chaman's age

Aman's age 3 years from now = 2 × Chaman's age

**Formula Used:**

Past Age = Present Age − Time Gap

Future Age = Present Age + Time Gap

 3 Years Ago A : C = 4 : 1 3 Years Hence A : C = 6 : 3 
• 
 +6 Years Ratio Method Aman parts: 6 − 4 = 2 2 parts = 6 years 1 part = 3 years Past Age = 4 × 3 = 12 Present Age = 15 yrs 

**Calculations:**

Let Aman's present age be A and Chaman's present age be C.

According to the first condition (3 years ago):

⇒ A − 3 = 4(C − 3)

⇒ A − 4C = −12 + 3

⇒ A − 4C = −9 ... (Equation 1)

According to the second condition (3 years from now):

⇒ A + 3 = 2(C + 3)

⇒ A − 2C = 6 − 3

⇒ A − 2C = 3 ... (Equation 2)

Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (A − 2C) − (A − 4C) = 3 − (−9)

⇒ 2C = 12

⇒ C = 6

Substitute C = 6 in Equation 2:

⇒ A − 2(6) = 3

⇒ A − 12 = 3

⇒ A = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference in ages between any two individuals always remains constant over time. This vital property is used to balance the ratios of their ages in different time periods.

Cross-Multiplication Method for Ages

If an initial age ratio a : b changes to c : d after a gap of T years, the exact value of 1 ratio part can be calculated directly as [T(c − d)] ÷ (ad − bc).

Ratio Equalization Method

To equate the ratio gaps horizontally, calculate the numerical difference between the terms of each ratio. Multiply the first ratio by the difference of the second, and vice versa.

questions.question: Mohammad Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi founded which of the following movements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deoband Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deoband Movement** was founded by **Mohammad Qasim Nanotavi** and **Rashid Ahmed Gangohi** in **1866** at Deoband, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• It was established with the aim of **reviving Islamic teachings** and promoting Islamic education in India.
 
• The movement primarily focused on the establishment of the **Darul Uloom Deoband**, an Islamic seminary that became a key center for the dissemination of Islamic knowledge and ideology.
 
• The founders opposed the influence of British colonial rule and sought to **preserve Islamic culture and traditions** in India.
 
• The movement emphasized **Quranic education** and the teachings of the Hadith while rejecting Western influences and modernist interpretations of Islam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of the Deoband Movement:**

 
 
• The Deoband Movement was rooted in **Islamic orthodoxy** and aimed at countering the spread of Western education and Christian missionary activities.
 
• The movement was based on the principles of **Wahhabi ideology**, although it adapted certain elements to suit the Indian context.
 
• Its primary goal was to train Islamic scholars (ulama) who could spread and uphold Islamic teachings in society.
 
• The teachings at Darul Uloom Deoband emphasized a strict adherence to Islamic law (**Sharia**) and the rejection of innovations (bid'ah) in religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Darul Uloom Deoband:**
 
 
• Established in **1866**, Darul Uloom Deoband became one of the most influential Islamic seminaries in the world.
 
• The curriculum combined traditional Islamic sciences with modern pedagogical methods to produce well-rounded Islamic scholars.
 
• The institution played a significant role in the **freedom struggle against British colonial rule**, as many of its scholars actively participated in India's independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Wahabi Movement:** This was a revivalist movement inspired by the teachings of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab in Arabia, emphasizing a return to the pure form of Islam. It was spearheaded in India by **Syed Ahmed Barelvi**.
 
• **Pagal Panthi Movement:** This was a socio-religious movement in Bengal led by **Karam Shah** and later his son **Tipu Shah**, focusing on the rights of peasants and the poor.
 
• **Shariya Movement:** This is a general term referring to efforts to implement or promote **Islamic law (Sharia)** in various contexts, but it is not specifically linked to the Deoband founders.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Deoband Movement:**
 
 
• The movement significantly influenced Islamic education and scholarship across South Asia and other parts of the world.
 
• It inspired the establishment of numerous Islamic seminaries and institutions globally that follow the Deobandi ideology.
 
• The movement continues to have a strong impact on Islamic jurisprudence and education in many Muslim-majority and minority countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Deoband Movement** was instrumental in preserving Islamic identity during a period of significant socio-political changes under British colonial rule.
 
• Its teachings emphasized the importance of adhering to the **Hanafi school of Islamic jurisprudence**.
 
• Many Islamic political and religious movements in South Asia, such as the **Tablighi Jamaat**, have their roots in the Deobandi tradition.
 
• The movement's scholars actively opposed British policies and were key participants in movements such as the **Khilafat Movement** and the **Indian National Congress**.

questions.question: Which of the following observations indicates that a chemical reaction has taken place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **change in temperature** is one of the most common indications that a chemical reaction has occurred. It signifies that energy has either been released (exothermic reaction) or absorbed (endothermic reaction).
 
• In chemical reactions, the formation of new substances involves breaking and forming chemical bonds, which often involves an exchange of energy in the form of heat. This is observed as a change in temperature.
 
• For example, when quicklime (calcium oxide) reacts with water, it produces calcium hydroxide and releases heat, causing the mixture to become hot. This is an exothermic reaction.
 
• Similarly, in endothermic reactions, such as the decomposition of calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, heat is absorbed, and the surroundings may feel cooler.
 
• Other changes such as a change in texture, size, or shape are generally physical changes and do not confirm the occurrence of a chemical reaction. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indicators of a chemical reaction:**

 
 
• **Change in color:** Some chemical reactions result in a noticeable change in color. For example, when iron rusts, it changes from a metallic gray to a reddish-brown color due to the formation of iron oxide.
 
• **Evolution of gas:** The formation of gas bubbles during a reaction, such as in the reaction between vinegar (acetic acid) and baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), indicates a chemical reaction.
 
• **Precipitate formation:** A precipitate is a solid that forms from a solution during a chemical reaction. For instance, when solutions of silver nitrate and sodium chloride are mixed, silver chloride precipitates out.
 
• **Change in smell:** A new odor may be produced during a chemical reaction, such as when food spoils or burns.
 
• **Emission of light:** Some reactions release energy in the form of light, such as the combustion of magnesium ribbon, which produces a bright white flame.
 
 
 
• **Physical changes vs. chemical changes:**
 
 
• **Physical changes** involve changes in the physical state or appearance of a substance without altering its chemical composition. Examples include melting, freezing, and breaking.
 
• **Chemical changes** result in the formation of new substances with different chemical properties. Examples include rusting, combustion, and digestion.
 
 
 
• **Examples of exothermic and endothermic reactions:**
 
 
• **Exothermic reactions:** Combustion of fuels, neutralization reactions between acids and bases, and the condensation of water vapor.
 
• **Endothermic reactions:** Photosynthesis, melting of ice, and evaporation of water.
 
 
 
• **Applications of temperature change in chemical reactions:**
 
 
• In industries, exothermic reactions are used for heat generation, such as in combustion engines.
 
• Endothermic reactions are exploited in cooling applications, such as instant cold packs used in sports injuries.
 
• Monitoring temperature changes in reactions can help chemists understand reaction kinetics and optimize processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exothermic reactions:** Reactions where heat is released into the surroundings, often causing a rise in temperature.
 
• **Endothermic reactions:** Reactions that absorb heat from the surroundings, causing a drop in temperature.
 
• **Chemical energy:** The energy stored in the chemical bonds of substances, which is either released or absorbed during a reaction.
 
• **Examples in daily life:** Cooking food involves endothermic reactions, while burning wood in a fireplace is an example of an exothermic reaction.

questions.question: Speakers of which of the following languages in India are mostly confined to the Himalayan belt contiguous with the international boundaries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tibeto-Burman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tibeto-Burman languages** are predominantly spoken by communities residing in the **Himalayan belt of India**, which is contiguous with international boundaries like China, Bhutan, Nepal, and Myanmar.
 
• These languages are primarily spoken in regions such as **Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Manipur**.
 
• The Tibeto-Burman languages belong to the larger Sino-Tibetan language family, which is one of the world's major language families.
 
• Communities speaking these languages are often ethnic minorities with distinct cultural and linguistic identities, many of which are influenced by their proximity to neighboring Himalayan countries.
 
• Some prominent examples of Tibeto-Burman languages include **Bodo, Lepcha, Meitei (Manipuri), Garo, and Naga languages**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indo-Aryan Languages:**

 
 
• The Indo-Aryan languages are a branch of the Indo-European language family and are the most widely spoken language group in India.
 
• They include major languages such as **Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, Marathi, Gujarati, and Odia**, primarily spoken in the northern, central, and western parts of India.
 
• Unlike Tibeto-Burman languages, Indo-Aryan languages are not confined to the Himalayan belt.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Languages:**
 
 
• Dravidian languages are primarily spoken in southern India and include prominent languages such as **Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam**.
 
• They are not geographically connected to the Himalayan region, as they are mainly centered in the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
 
 
• **Austric Languages:**
 
 
• Austric or Austroasiatic languages are spoken by tribal communities in eastern and central India, such as the **Santhals, Mundas, and Khasis**.
 
• These languages are primarily found in regions like **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and the Northeastern states**, but they are not concentrated in the Himalayan belt.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Tibeto-Burman Languages:**
 
 
• The Tibeto-Burman languages are **tonal**, meaning the meaning of a word can change based on the pitch or tone used while pronouncing it.
 
• They have **rich oral traditions**, and many languages lack a written script, relying on oral storytelling and folklore.
 
• These languages are often influenced by the cultural and political interactions with **Tibetan, Chinese, and Southeast Asian cultures**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Tibeto-Burman language family has ancient roots and has been present in the Himalayan region for thousands of years.
 
• Migration patterns from **Tibet and Southeast Asia** significantly shaped the linguistic landscape of the region.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Many Tibeto-Burman languages are endangered due to the dominance of larger languages like Hindi and English, leading to a decline in native speakers.
 
• Efforts by government and cultural organizations are underway to **document and preserve these languages**.

questions.question:
Simplify the expression given below.

3⁵-((1)/(3))⁻⁵+sqrt{frac{27¹²+9¹³}{27⁶+9¹⁴}}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all bases directly to 3 to simplify.

⇒ 3⁵ − 3⁵ + √[(3³⁶ + 3²⁶) ÷ (3¹⁸ + 3²⁸)]

⇒ 0 + √[{3²⁶(3¹⁰ + 1)} ÷ {3¹⁸(1 + 3¹⁰)}]

⇒ √(3⁸) = 3⁴ = 81

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

3⁵ − (1/3)−⁵ + √[(27¹² + 9¹³) ÷ (27⁶ + 9¹⁴)]

**Formulas Used:**

⇒ (am)ⁿ = amⁿ

⇒ am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

⇒ a−m = 1 ÷ am

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, evaluate the first two terms:

⇒ (1/3)−⁵ = (3−¹)−⁵ = 3⁵

⇒ 3⁵ − 3⁵ = 0

⇒ Second, evaluate the fraction inside the square root by converting bases to 3:

⇒ Numerator: 27¹² + 9¹³ = (3³)¹² + (3²)¹³ = 3³⁶ + 3²⁶

⇒ Denominator: 27⁶ + 9¹⁴ = (3³)⁶ + (3²)¹⁴ = 3¹⁸ + 3²⁸

⇒ Take out the common minimum powers from numerator and denominator:

⇒ Fraction = [3²⁶(3¹⁰ + 1)] ÷ [3¹⁸(1 + 3¹⁰)]

⇒ Cancel out the common term (3¹⁰ + 1):

⇒ Fraction = 3²⁶ ÷ 3¹⁸

⇒ Fraction = 3²⁶−¹⁸ = 3⁸

⇒ Finally, substitute back into the full expression:

⇒ 0 + √(3⁸)

⇒ 3⁴ = 81

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Laws of Exponents (Multiplication & Division)

When multiplying terms with the same base, add their powers: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ. When dividing, subtract the powers: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ.

Negative Exponents

A negative exponent indicates the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive power: a−m = 1 ÷ am or (a/b)−m = (b/a)m.

Power of a Power Rule

When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents: (am)ⁿ = amⁿ. This is especially useful for converting composite bases to prime bases.

Fractional Exponents and Roots

The square root of a term can be written as a fractional exponent: √a = a¹/². Therefore, √(am) = am/².

questions.question: If A and B together can finish a job in 10 days, and B alone can finish it in 15 days, how many days will A alone take to finish the job?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If A and B together take 'x' days and B alone takes 'y' days, A alone will take (x × y) ÷ (y − x) days.

Here, x = 10 days and y = 15 days.

Time taken by A = (10 × 15) ÷ (15 − 10)

Time taken by A = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 10 days

Time taken by B alone = 15 days

Pipes and Cisterns

Work and Wages

questions.question: Simplify: x(5x - 5) + 7(x² - 2) + 15 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expand the expression directly using the distributive property:

⇒ 5x² − 5x + 7x² − 14 + 15

Combine the like terms:

⇒ 12x² − 5x + 1

**∴ The correct answer is 12x² − 5x + 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: x(5x − 5) + 7(x² − 2) + 15

**Calculations:**

Multiply the terms outside the brackets with the terms inside:

⇒ (x × 5x) − (x × 5) + (7 × x²) − (7 × 2) + 15

⇒ 5x² − 5x + 7x² − 14 + 15

Group the x² terms, x terms, and constant values together:

⇒ (5x² + 7x²) − 5x + (15 − 14)

Add the coefficients of the like terms:

⇒ 12x² − 5x + 1

**∴ The correct answer is 12x² − 5x + 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distributive Property

The distributive property states that multiplying a sum by a number gives the same result as multiplying each addend by the number. Rule: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

Combining Like Terms

Like terms are terms that contain the same variables raised to the exact same powers. They can be simplified by adding or subtracting their numerical coefficients.

BODMAS Rule

BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division / Multiplication, and Addition / Subtraction. It sets the strict order of operations for solving any mathematical expression.

• **Examples of Cases Resolved:**
 
 
• Motor vehicle accident compensation cases settled amicably between the claimant and insurance companies.
 
• Family disputes resolved through mutual agreement, avoiding lengthy legal battles.
 
• Bank recovery cases where borrowers and banks negotiate repayment terms.
 
• Compoundable criminal cases resolved through compromise between parties.

questions.question: A train travels three equal distances of 180 km each at speeds of 45 km/hr, 60 km/hr and 90 km/hr, respectively. What is the total time taken to cover all three distances?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total time is simply the sum of the individual times taken for each segment.

Total Time = (Distance₁ ÷ Speed₁) + (Distance₂ ÷ Speed₂) + (Distance₃ ÷ Speed₃)

Total Time = (180 ÷ 45) + (180 ÷ 60) + (180 ÷ 90)

Total Time = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Distance of each segment = 180 km

Speeds for each segment = 45 km/hr, 60 km/hr, and 90 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = t₁ + t₂ + t₃

 180 km 180 km 180 km 45 km/hr 60 km/hr 90 km/hr Time = 4 hrs Time = 3 hrs Time = 2 hrs Total Time = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 hours 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time for first segment (t₁) = 180 ÷ 45 = 4 hours

⇒ Time for second segment (t₂) = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours

⇒ Time for third segment (t₃) = 180 ÷ 90 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Time = 4 + 3 + 2

⇒ Total Time = 9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hours.**

Average Speed

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Proportionality in Time, Speed and Distance

If distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional (S ∝ 1/T). If time is constant, Distance and Speed are directly proportional (D ∝ S).

• The **Returning Officer supervises all polling stations** within their constituency and ensures that the election is conducted in accordance with the guidelines laid out by the Election Commission of India.

• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional authority responsible for administering elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President of India.
 
• It ensures free, fair, and transparent elections across the country.
 
• The Commission appoints Returning Officers and other officials to execute the election process efficiently.

H.C.F. of Fractions

questions.question: The period of southwest monsoon from _______ is known as the rainy season for most parts of the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**June to September**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Southwest monsoon** is a significant climatic phenomenon in India, marking the rainy season for most parts of the country. It occurs between **June and September**.
 
• This period accounts for approximately **75-90% of India's annual rainfall**, making it crucial for agriculture and water resources.
 
• The monsoon is driven by the seasonal reversal of wind systems and the difference in temperature between land and sea, causing moist winds from the Indian Ocean to sweep across the subcontinent.
 
• Regions such as the Western Ghats, northeastern states, and the Indo-Gangetic plains receive heavy rainfall during this period, benefiting agriculture and replenishing water bodies.
 
• The **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)** monitors the onset, progression, and retreat of the monsoon season to aid in disaster preparedness and agricultural planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Southwest Monsoon Mechanism:**

 
 
• The monsoon originates due to the **differential heating** of land and sea. The intense heat over the Indian subcontinent creates low-pressure areas, attracting moist winds from the Indian Ocean.
 
• The winds are deflected due to the **Coriolis effect**, resulting in their southwest direction.
 
 
 
• **Regional Impacts of the Monsoon:**
 
 
• Regions such as **Kerala** experience the onset of the monsoon in early June, followed by other parts of the country.
 
• Northeastern states, including **Meghalaya**, receive some of the highest rainfall globally during this period.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Importance:**
 
 
• India's agriculture is predominantly **monsoon-dependent**, with crops like rice, sugarcane, and cotton relying heavily on monsoon rains.
 
• A delayed or weak monsoon can lead to **drought conditions**, affecting crop yields and the economy.
 
 
 
• **Retreat of the Monsoon:**
 
 
• The withdrawal of the monsoon begins in **September**, starting from the northwest region and gradually retreating southward.
 
• Post-monsoon showers, also known as **retreating monsoon**, are common in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monsoon Forecasting:**

 
 
• The **Indian Meteorological Department (IMD)** provides monsoon forecasts based on various models, including dynamical and statistical ones.
 
• Accurate forecasting helps in planning **agricultural activities**, managing water resources, and preparing for potential disasters like floods.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Impacts:**
 
 
• Studies indicate that **climate change** is affecting the monsoon patterns, leading to uneven distribution of rainfall.
 
• Extreme events such as **floods** and **droughts** are becoming more frequent due to changing monsoon dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Global Connections:**
 
 
• The Indian monsoon is part of a larger atmospheric circulation system and is influenced by phenomena like **El Niño** and **La Niña**.
 
• **El Niño** events generally weaken the monsoon, while **La Niña** enhances it.

questions.question: Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) registration may be cancelled if _______.

options.text: The Overseas Citizen of India formally seeks dual citizenship status
The Overseas Citizen of India permanently relocates to another country
The Overseas Citizen of India violates the Citizenship Act or any notified law
The Overseas Citizen of India refuses to comply with tax obligations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Overseas Citizen of India violates the Citizenship Act or any notified law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019** stipulates that the registration of an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) can be cancelled if the individual violates **any provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955** or any other **notified law**.
 
• Section 7D of the **Citizenship Act, 1955** provides the legal grounds for cancellation of OCI registration, including cases where the person has acted against the sovereignty, integrity, security, or interests of India.
 
• The cancellation of OCI registration is typically reserved for **serious violations** of laws, which may include acts that jeopardize national security, public order, or the rule of law in India.
 
• Such cancellation is conducted through a due process and is subject to an **opportunity for the individual to present their case** before the authorities.
 
• It is essential for OCI holders to comply with Indian laws and regulations, as the OCI status does not grant immunity from legal consequences in case of violations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Scheme:**

 
 
• OCI is a **long-term visa** scheme introduced by the Government of India under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
• It allows persons of Indian origin residing abroad to enjoy certain rights in India, such as visa-free travel and exemption from registration with police authorities for stays longer than 180 days.
 
• OCI cardholders can engage in activities such as buying property and pursuing education in India but are restricted from voting, holding public office, and working in government jobs.
 
 
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019:**
 
 
• The act amended the **Citizenship Act, 1955** to provide Indian citizenship to persecuted minorities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians) from **Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh** who entered India before December 31, 2014.
 
• It excludes certain categories such as **Muslims** and has been a subject of political and social debates.
 
 
 
• **Key Restrictions for OCI Cardholders:**
 
 
• OCI holders are prohibited from **voting in Indian elections**, holding constitutional posts, or acquiring agricultural properties.
 
• They cannot participate in political activities or work in government sectors.
 
• Any violation of Indian laws, especially those affecting sovereignty or security, could lead to the cancellation of OCI registration.
 
 
 
• **Section 7D of Citizenship Act, 1955:**
 
 
• It defines the circumstances under which the registration of an OCI can be cancelled, including:
 
 
• If the registration was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.
 
• If the individual violates **any provisions of the Citizenship Act** or other laws notified by the central government.
 
• If the individual has shown disloyalty or hostility towards India.
 
 
 
• Cancellation under Section 7D is subject to **legal procedures**, ensuring that the individual has a chance to defend themselves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cancellation Process:**

 
 
• OCI registration can only be cancelled after following a due process, including providing the individual with an opportunity to explain their actions.
 
• The decision is taken by the **central government**, and the reasons for cancellation must be clearly documented.
 
 
 
• **Safeguards for OCI Holders:**
 
 
• The cancellation of OCI registration is a serious action and is not undertaken for minor infractions or violations.
 
• It is reserved for cases involving fraud, severe legal violations, or actions against national interests.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, along with its amendments, provides the legal basis for managing citizenship and OCI registrations.
 
• Section 7D of the act is pivotal in defining the grounds and procedures for cancellation.

questions.question: The 7-digit number 40A861B is divisible by 3. What is the minimum value of (A + B)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of the known digits = 4 + 0 + 8 + 6 + 1 = 19.

To be divisible by 3, the total sum of all digits must be a multiple of 3.

The smallest multiple of 3 greater than 19 is 21.

∴ Minimum sum of (A + B) = 21 − 19 = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A 7-digit number 40A861B is divisible by 3.

**Concept Used:**

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is perfectly divisible by 3.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum of the digits = 4 + 0 + A + 8 + 6 + 1 + B

⇒ Sum of the digits = 19 + A + B

⇒ For the number to be perfectly divisible by 3, the expression (19 + A + B) must be divisible by 3.

⇒ The possible multiples of 3 greater than or equal to 19 are 21, 24, 27, 30, etc.

⇒ To find the minimum value of (A + B), we equate the sum to the smallest possible multiple of 3, which is 21.

⇒ 19 + A + B = 21

⇒ A + B = 21 − 19

⇒ A + B = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its individual digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: Which of the following is the longest river in the desert region of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Luni** is the longest river in the desert region of India, flowing through the arid areas of **Rajasthan** and **Gujarat**. It is approximately **495 km** in length.
 
• The Luni River originates from the **Naga Hills** in the Aravalli range, near Ajmer in Rajasthan, and flows southwest towards the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
 
• It is an ephemeral river, meaning it carries water only during the monsoon season, making it a crucial water source for the region.
 
• The river is saline in nature due to the high salt content in the desert soil, and its name "Luni" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Lavanavari," meaning "salt river."
 
• Unlike perennial rivers such as the Yamuna, Ganga, and Brahmaputra, which have year-round water flow, Luni is specifically significant for the desert ecosystem, supporting agriculture and livelihoods in the region.
 
• The other options provided in the question—**Yamuna, Ganga, and Brahmaputra**—are perennial rivers and are not located in the desert regions of India. Hence, they are incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Luni River – Characteristics:**

 
 
• The Luni River basin covers an area of approximately **37,363 square kilometers**.
 
• Its major tributaries include the **Jojari, Sukri, Jawai, and Bandi rivers**, which contribute to its flow.
 
• The river does not drain into any sea or ocean; instead, it ends in the marshy lands of the **Rann of Kutch**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Other Rivers:**
 
 
• **Yamuna:** A major tributary of the Ganga, it flows through northern Indian states and is not located in the desert region.
 
• **Ganga:** One of India’s holiest rivers, originating from the Himalayas, flows through the Indo-Gangetic plains and is perennial.
 
• **Brahmaputra:** Originates in Tibet, flows through Assam and Bangladesh, and is known for its vast size and perennial nature.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Desert Rivers:**
 
 
• Desert rivers like Luni provide critical water resources for irrigation, drinking water, and livestock in arid regions.
 
• They support the sparse vegetation and unique ecosystems of the desert areas.
 
 
 
• **Salinity in Luni River:**
 
 
• The high salinity of the river water is due to the evaporation of water and the accumulation of salts from the desert soil.
 
• This makes the water unsuitable for drinking but usable for certain types of salt-tolerant crops.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ephemeral Nature:** The Luni River flows only during the monsoon, highlighting the importance of water conservation and storage in desert regions.
 
• **Salt Production:** The salinity of Luni supports the small-scale salt production industry in the region.
 
• **Desert Ecosystem:** Desert rivers like Luni play a vital role in supporting the fragile ecosystems of arid zones by maintaining biodiversity and providing water for flora and fauna.

questions.question: Atul earns ₹16,000 per month. He spends ₹5,500 on rent, ₹2,500 on bills, and saves the remaining amount each month. If he uses his entire monthly savings for his birthday celebration in one month, find his total savings for the year (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Monthly expenses = 5500 + 2500 = ₹8000

Monthly savings = Income − Expenses = 16000 − 8000 = ₹8000

He spends 1 month's savings, so he effectively saves for 11 months.

Total yearly savings = 8000 × 11 = ₹88000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹88000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Monthly salary of Atul = ₹16,000

Monthly rent spent = ₹5,500

Monthly bills paid = ₹2,500

**Formula Used:**

Total Income = Total Expenditure + Savings

Annual Savings = Monthly Savings × Number of Saving Months

 Monthly Income: ₹16,000 Expenses: ₹8,000 Savings: ₹8,000 Annual Savings = ₹8,000 × 11 Months 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total monthly expenditure = Rent + Bills

⇒ Total monthly expenditure = 5500 + 2500 = ₹8,000

⇒ Monthly savings = Total Income − Total Expenditure

⇒ Monthly savings = 16000 − 8000 = ₹8,000

⇒ Number of months in a full year = 12

⇒ Since he spent his entire savings in one month for his birthday celebration, the number of months he successfully saved is: 12 − 1 = 11 months

⇒ Total savings for the year = Monthly savings × 11

⇒ Total savings = 8000 × 11 = ₹88,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹88000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Principle

Income is the aggregate of all expenses and savings. Any change in income or expenditure directly reflects on the savings proportionally. The core relationship is always Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Effective Annual Evaluation

• He was a powerful ruler who consolidated his authority by defeating several contemporary rulers, including the **Gurjara Pratiharas**, the **Pala dynasty** rulers, and others in the Indian subcontinent.

__
 
• **Eleventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** was introduced by the **73rd Amendment Act** in **1992**. It deals with the **powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats**.
 
• The Eleventh Schedule contains a list of **29 functional items** that are to be devolved to the Panchayats. These items include areas like agriculture, irrigation, education, health, sanitation, and rural development.
 
• The inclusion of the Eleventh Schedule aims to strengthen **decentralized governance** and ensure that local self-government operates efficiently.
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act** institutionalized Panchayati Raj in India, empowering rural local bodies to manage economic development and social justice.
 
• Under this schedule, **state legislatures** are tasked with determining the powers and functions of Panchayats concerning the items listed.

• It lists **18 functional items** such as urban planning, regulation of land use, water supply, sanitation, and public health.
 
 
 
• **Tenth Schedule:**

• It provides provisions to disqualify members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the grounds of defection.
 
 
 
• **Ninth Schedule:**
 
 
• The **Ninth Schedule** was introduced by the **First Amendment Act** of **1951**. It contains laws that are exempt from judicial review to protect land reform and other socio-economic measures.
 
• It primarily aimed at safeguarding laws that were in conflict with the Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **73rd and 74th Amendments:**
 
 
• The **73rd Amendment Act** institutionalized Panchayati Raj, while the **74th Amendment Act** focused on Municipalities.
 
• These amendments aimed to promote grassroots-level governance and decentralized administration across rural and urban areas.

• Promotes **participatory democracy** at the grassroots level.
 
• Facilitates **accountability and transparency** in rural governance.

• Three-tier system comprising **Gram Panchayat**, **Panchayat Samiti**, and **Zilla Parishad**.
 
• Election of members through **universal adult suffrage**.
 
• Reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes**, **Scheduled Tribes**, and **women**.

questions.question: Which of the following laws states that 'Every object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's First Law of Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion** states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. This is also known as the **Law of Inertia**.
 
• This law implies that objects have a natural tendency to maintain their current state of motion unless influenced by an unbalanced force.
 
• The principle is fundamental to understanding the concept of inertia, which is the resistance of an object to change its state of motion or rest.
 
• For example, a book lying on a table will remain stationary unless a force, like a push, is applied to it, or a moving car will continue in motion unless brakes or friction are applied to stop it.
 
• This law is the foundation for analyzing motion and forces in classical mechanics, making it essential in physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:**

 
 
• This law states that the total momentum of a closed system of objects (with no external forces acting) remains constant over time.
 
• It is mathematically expressed as: **m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = constant**, where m and v represent mass and velocity of objects, respectively.
 
• This principle is critical in collision and explosion analyses.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion:**
 
 
• This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• It explains phenomena like the recoil of a gun when fired or the propulsion of a rocket.
 
• Example: If you push against a wall, the wall pushes back with an equal and opposite force.
 
 
 
• **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion:**
 
 
• These laws describe the motion of planets around the Sun.
 
• They include:
 
 
• The Law of Ellipses (planets move in elliptical orbits).
 
• The Law of Equal Areas (a line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas during equal intervals of time).
 
• The Harmonic Law (the square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit).
 
 
 
 
 
• **Inertia:**
 
 
• Inertia is the property of an object to resist changes in its state of motion or rest.
 
• It depends on the object's mass; higher mass means greater inertia.
 
• Example: A heavy truck requires more force to accelerate or decelerate compared to a small car.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• Newton's First Law builds on Galileo's concept of inertia, which was formulated during his experiments with inclined planes.
 
• Galileo proposed that in the absence of friction, a moving object would continue moving indefinitely.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding why seat belts are necessary in cars to protect passengers during sudden stops or collisions.
 
• Explains why objects in space continue moving without any propulsion due to the lack of external forces like friction.
 
 
 
• **Practical Observations:**
 
 
• When a bus suddenly stops, passengers tend to lurch forward due to inertia.
 
• Objects on a conveyor belt in factories remain stationary until external forces act upon them.
