questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: The acquisition of education and knowledge
The standard of living and command over resources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Military strength and defence expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite statistical measure used to rank countries based on human development levels. It considers three major dimensions: **Health, Education, and Standard of Living**.
 
• **A long and healthy life:** This dimension is measured using indicators such as **life expectancy at birth**. It highlights the overall health and longevity of the population. *Hence, this is part of HDI.*
 
• **The acquisition of education and knowledge:** This dimension is assessed by indicators like **mean years of schooling** and **expected years of schooling**, reflecting the educational achievements of the population. *Hence, this is part of HDI.*
 
• **The standard of living and command over resources:** This dimension is measured using **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, which indicates the economic prosperity and living conditions of the people. *Hence, this is part of HDI.*
 
• **Military strength and defence expenditure** is not a dimension of HDI. HDI focuses on factors that directly contribute to human development and quality of life rather than a nation's military capabilities or defence spending. *Hence, this is NOT part of HDI.*
 
• HDI was introduced by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its **Human Development Report (HDR) in 1990**, aiming to shift focus from economic statistics to people-centric development metrics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions of HDI:**

 
 
• **Health:** Measured by **life expectancy at birth**, indicating the ability to lead a long and healthy life.
 
• **Education:** Assessed through **mean years of schooling** (average education received by the population) and **expected years of schooling** (anticipated education for children entering school).
 
• **Standard of Living:** Measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, reflecting economic well-being and access to resources.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of HDI:**
 
 
• HDI is calculated using a geometric mean of normalized indices for each of the three dimensions: **Health, Education, and Standard of Living**.
 
• The **UNDP** publishes HDI rankings annually for countries worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Global HDI Rankings:**
 
 
• Countries with high HDI scores, such as **Norway, Switzerland, and Ireland**, typically have excellent healthcare systems, high educational attainment, and strong economies.
 
• Countries with lower HDI scores often face challenges in areas like health infrastructure, access to education, and poverty.
 
 
 
• **Other Indices Related to Development:**
 
 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII):** Measures inequality in achievements between men and women in reproductive health, empowerment, and economic activity.
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):** Assesses poverty beyond income-based measures, considering factors like health, education, and living standards.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin:** The HDI was developed by **Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq** and **Indian economist Amartya Sen** to emphasize people-centric development.
 
• **HDI Categories:** Countries are categorized into **Very High, High, Medium, and Low Human Development** based on their HDI scores.
 
• **Limitations:** HDI does not consider inequalities, gender disparities, or ecological sustainability, which are increasingly significant for evaluating development.
 
• **India’s HDI Rank:** As of the latest report, India ranks in the **medium human development category**, with significant improvements in life expectancy and education indicators.

• **ASCII** stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, which is a character encoding standard used in computers and other electronic devices for representing text.
 
• It was first developed in the **1960s** by the American National Standards Institute (**ANSI**) to standardize text representation across different platforms and devices.
 
• **ASCII** uses a 7-bit binary code to represent **128 unique characters**, including uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, punctuation marks, and special control characters like newline or tab.
 
• The standard is widely used in programming, data communication, and text files, as it ensures compatibility between systems.
 
• **Extended ASCII** variants expand the character set to **256 characters** by using 8 bits, enabling support for additional symbols and language-specific characters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Development of ASCII:**

 
 
• **ASCII** was developed by a committee led by Robert W. Bemer in the early 1960s to create a standard for encoding text in digital systems.
 
• It was approved in 1963 and revised in **1967** to include the lowercase alphabet and additional symbols.
 
 
 
• **Applications of ASCII:**
 
 
• Widely used in **programming languages** like C and Python for text processing.
 
• Essential in **internet protocols** like HTTP, SMTP, and FTP for communication between systems.
 
• Used in **plain text files** (.txt) and in encoding data for transfer between different platforms.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of ASCII:**
 
 
• Uses a **7-bit binary representation**, allowing 128 unique character codes.
 
• Includes printable characters like letters, digits, and symbols, as well as control characters like **line feed** and **carriage return**.
 
• It is **platform-independent**, making it ideal for cross-platform compatibility.
 
 
 
• **Extended ASCII and Unicode:**
 
 
• **Extended ASCII** uses 8 bits to represent 256 characters, adding support for language-specific characters and symbols.
 
• **Unicode** is a modern standard that builds upon ASCII, supporting over **143,000 characters** from various scripts and symbols worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Control Characters:**

 
 
• ASCII includes control characters like **NULL (0)**, **Start of Header (SOH)**, and **End of Transmission (EOT)**, which are used in data communication.
 
• These characters are non-printable and are used for signaling and formatting.
 
 
 
• **ASCII Table:**
 
 
• The **ASCII table** maps characters to their corresponding decimal, hexadecimal, and binary codes.
 
• For example, the letter **'A'** corresponds to **65 (decimal)** or **01000001 (binary)**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy and Compatibility:**
 
 
• Despite the rise of Unicode, ASCII remains widely used in legacy systems and for basic text processing.
 
• Its simplicity and universal adoption make it a foundational standard in computing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three approaches of the Government of India for poverty reduction?

options.text: Growth-oriented approach with the expectation that economic growth would trickle down to the poor.
Raise incomes and employment for the poor by creating additional assets and by means of work generation.
Ensure the bare minimum level of remuneration or wage for labour with different levels of skills.
Provide minimum basic amenities to people through public expenditure on social consumption needs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ensure the bare minimum level of remuneration or wage for labour with different levels of skills.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India has adopted **three primary approaches** for poverty reduction:
 
• **Growth-oriented approach:** Focuses on economic growth with the belief that the benefits of growth will trickle down to the poor. *Hence, this approach is correct.*
 
• **Asset creation and employment generation:** Aims to raise incomes and employment for the poor by creating additional assets and generating work opportunities. *Hence, this approach is correct.*
 
• **Provision of basic amenities:** Ensures access to minimum basic amenities such as healthcare, education, and housing through public expenditure on social consumption needs. *Hence, this approach is correct.*
 
• The **statement about ensuring the bare minimum remuneration** for labour is not a comprehensive poverty reduction strategy but rather a labour policy initiative under minimum wage laws. Therefore, it **does not qualify** as one of the three approaches. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Growth-Oriented Approach:**

 
 
• This approach emphasizes economic growth as a means to reduce poverty.
 
• The idea is to generate wealth and increase income levels, which will eventually benefit the poor.
 
• For example, liberalization policies initiated in **1991** focused on economic growth, indirectly reducing poverty.
 
 
 
• **Asset Creation and Employment Generation:**
 
 
• Programs like the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005**, aim to provide rural employment and create durable assets.
 
• Such schemes are targeted at improving the livelihood of the poorest sections of society by generating work opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Provision of Basic Amenities:**
 
 
• Programs such as **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, and **National Health Mission (NHM)** ensure access to housing, sanitation, and healthcare for the poor.
 
• These initiatives aim to improve the living standards of people below the poverty line by addressing their basic needs.
 
 
 
• **Minimum Wage Laws:**
 
 
• The statement about ensuring a bare minimum remuneration for labour is a reference to labour laws like the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**.
 
• This act ensures that workers are paid at least the minimum wage for their work based on skill levels, preventing exploitation.
 
• While important, it is not classified as a poverty reduction strategy but as a measure for ensuring fair labour practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **MGNREGA:** Provides at least **100 days of guaranteed wage employment** in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP):** Aims to provide support to aged, widowed, disabled, and families in extreme poverty through financial assistance.
 
• **Public Distribution System (PDS):** Ensures food security by distributing essential commodities like rice, wheat, and kerosene at subsidized prices.
 
• **Minimum Wages Act, 1948:** Protects workers from being underpaid by fixing minimum wages for different categories of work.

questions.question: At a health club, 55% of the members are women and 45% of the members are men. If the average age of the men is 95 years and the average age of the women is 85 years, what is the average age (in years) of all the members?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of women to men = 55% : 45% = 11 : 9.

Assume the base average is 85 years (women's average).

Deviation of men's average from base = 95 − 85 = +10 years.

Total extra deviation = 9 parts × 10 = +90.

Increase in overall average = 90 ÷ (11 + 9) = 90 ÷ 20 = 4.5 years.

Overall average = 85 + 4.5 = 89.5 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 89.5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of women in the club = 55%

Percentage of men in the club = 45%

Average age of men = 95 years

Average age of women = 85 years

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 
• Women (55%) Avg: 85 Ratio: 11 Men (45%) Avg: 95 Ratio: 9 
• Total Average 
 9 parts gap 
 11 parts gap 
 Total Gap = 10 years (20 parts) 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of members in the health club be 100.

⇒ Number of women (n₁) = 55

⇒ Number of men (n₂) = 45

⇒ Ratio of women to men (n₁ : n₂) = 55 : 45 = 11 : 9

⇒ Total age of women = 11 × 85 = 935

⇒ Total age of men = 9 × 95 = 855

⇒ Total age of all members = 935 + 855 = 1790

⇒ Average age of all members = Total age ÷ Total ratio parts

⇒ Average age = 1790 ÷ (11 + 9) = 1790 ÷ 20 = 89.5 years

**∴ The correct answer is 89.5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when different groups have different sizes and distinct averages. Formula: Aw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂), where w represents the weight or count of the items.

Deviation Method

A calculation shortcut where an assumed mean is chosen, and the net deviation from this assumed mean is distributed equally among all elements. True Mean = Assumed Mean + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Total Count).

Alligation Method

An efficient cross-multiplication technique used to find the ratio in which two components are mixed. The gap between the component values and the average value creates inverse ratio proportions.
